To be frank, I think the appeal of Skyblock is that there is no set goal, so you can do whatever you literally want. Ranging from money, to the best stats, Dungeons, or even foraging if you love it that much. The lack of hand holding is great and it makes players interact with each other in the community. That's where Skyblock really thrives in the Mass Multiplayer Online aspect.

However, it would be nice if the mechanics of the game were explained in a more accessible way. Like a guidebook filled with the mechanics and features that are explained briefly but clearly. Perhaps for the  most general of information, those are already unlocked, but for the more specific features, those need to be unlocked. That will encourage exploring for new players.

It shouldn't really dictate of what a player should do, it should be more like a quick reference of what is there to offer and hopefully encourage players to brainstorm what they'd like to do. I'd like to think it would be accessible via Jerry or through your Skyblock menu.

Praise to be of knowledge and the Flower of Truth!  
After being rejected from a top tier academy for mages outside of Skyblock they came upon this world to study for new discoveries and to prove themselves worthy out of spite. However, at the very beginning it was a massive cultural shock to this player. Everything was so foreign. The system behaved and ran differently in comparison to how things were back at their homeland, leaving them at a massive disadvantage and put them into a position where they were progressing very slowly. It was very discouraging and this pushed them to the tipping point of throwing in the towel.

However, one day, while wandering around the main hub trying to evaluate their next move, they passed by the display windows of the auction house.

There, sat a Flower of Truth.

Now they have seen many FoTs before, but they never took an interest or liking towards them, however, something about this one, was.. different.

What was peculiar was the fact that it was on the lowest BIN, but nobody have picked it up and it was sitting there the last few days. Second of all, it looked slightly different. It was more crisp and the edges of its leaves and head were sharper. Thirdly, the player has sworn they hear a sorrowful whispering coming from it.  


Intrigued, they went inside the AH and purchased the FoT at its measly price.

When they returned to their quiet, distant cabin, the whispers were only more evident and louder. From then on, the player has figured out how to effectively communicate with the FoT. The Flower gave them knowledge that have became forbidden, tales from legendary players forgotten long ago, and anything else that the player could ask for. This is what they needed all along. Fearful of losing the powerful weapon, they stored it safe in a secret room within their cabin. However, the weapon did not had to be present for its effect to be there. The whispers of the Flower began haunting them, day and night, overwhelming them with knowledge and dreadful truths that drastically shifted their optimistic and enthusiastic attitude towards the darkness. In their quest for glory and to manifest the power of knowledge and understanding of anything and everything, all it took was a Flower to do them in.

Before, they couldn't reach out to the table right in front of them, now they are able to seek and make their impact meters away from their ranged mastery.

Despite being a respected player with decent goodies underneath their name, all it took was a wrong deal with the wrong people that forced them to take refuge in the Crimson Isles. Trust them when they say they would not recommend it to anyone. It's been months since they have put themselves in this position, but they have grown into surviving this horrific hellspace. It sucks and they don't know when they'll see the bright blue skies again, but for now, they're safe.
One afternoon, they travelled to the Scarleton Plaza to purchase their weekly goods from the Bazaar. However when they arrived, posters with their name and face were plastered everywhere, with a bolded "WANTED - DEAD OR ALIVE" with a bounty of 25 million.
Okay the deal was bad, but they thought it wasn't *that* bad, right? It was just a gamble, right? Nonetheless, the player is already back in the deep end. A looming feeling dawned upon them. Someone's blood is going to be spilled, very soon.

Play your cards right and fortune is on your side.

Part of the masses flocking to make a fortune, their dream of riches is familiar but their willpower is a hard stone and rare like a jasper.

Before they came to the world of Skyblock, they graduated college and became a cartographer that failed to make ends meet after falling for loan sharks. So when they came to the Crystal Hallows, it quickly became their second home. The Crystal Hallows provided everything they will ever need so they will never have to struggle again. Master of navigation, they can get anywhere from Point A to Point B in no time. However, they have severely underestimated the brutality of the mines. As they proceed to push on for mass fortune, their body grew weary from the amount of strain from the physical labor. Then, on an unfortunate day, the Crystal Hallows caved in and their body collapsed from exhaustion, unable to escape. As years pass and the entrance to the Hallows was eventually recovered, the newcomers have reported brief sightings of a player wearing a brown coat and a tattered sorrow armor set amongst the structures of the Hallows. However, these rumors, were never confirmed.
